facts.heading: GP suggested therapy visit
facts.content: Daniel's GP suggested he come to therapy because she observed he looked exhausted.
facts.evidence: My GP suggested I come. She said I look exhausted

facts.heading: Burnout started in October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burned out since October.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burned out since October

facts.heading: Workload increased since October
facts.content: Daniel's workload increased after the company lost a big client.
facts.evidence: We lost a big client, and half the team got moved onto the rescue plan

facts.heading: Daniel does three jobs
facts.content: Daniel ended up doing the jobs of three people.
facts.evidence: so I ended up doing three people's jobs

facts.heading: Works late into the night
facts.content: Daniel starts work at seven and still answers messages until ten at night.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by seven and I'm still answering messages at ten at night

facts.heading: Sleep duration is four hours
facts.content: Daniel sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours

facts.heading: Wakes up at three AM
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning and can't fall back asleep

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn

facts.heading: Father's age and condition
facts.content: Daniel's father is seventy-three years old.
facts.evidence: He's seventy-three and he's always been the strong one

facts.heading: Drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds

facts.heading: Appointments are every few weeks
facts.content: The neurology appointments for Daniel's father are every few weeks.
facts.evidence: The neurology appointments are every few weeks

facts.heading: Sister Hannah lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister, Hannah, lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto

facts.heading: Daniel feels guilty about care
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for even saying he is tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: I feel it's selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill

facts.heading: Tells sister he is fine
facts.content: Daniel tells his sister Hannah that he is fine when she asks how he is.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine

facts.heading: Cannot face hospital visits
facts.content: Daniel sometimes sits in the car park at the hospital for ten minutes before going in.
facts.evidence: some days I sit in the car park at the hospital for ten minutes before I go in

facts.heading: GP found stress and exhaustion
facts.content: Daniel's GP ran blood tests which were all normal. The GP attributed his symptoms to stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked therapy session
facts.content: Claire booked the therapy session for Daniel. Claire stated she was done watching him disappear.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked it, to be honest. Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.heading: Claire is patient but wearing
facts.content: Claire is very patient and makes Daniel tea without pushing him to talk. Daniel sees that this patience is wearing on her.
facts.evidence: I can see it's wearing on her too.

facts.heading: Avoids weekend trips with girlfriend
facts.content: Daniel has stopped accepting invitations from Claire to go away for the weekend. He feels worst about this.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend, because I always say no.

facts.heading: Work emails prevent rest
facts.content: Daniel feels that if he were away, he would return to two hundred emails. He is also concerned about his Dad needing something.
facts.evidence: If I'm away I'll come back to two hundred of them. And Dad might need something.

facts.heading: Stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago. He used to run ten kilometres every Saturday morning for six years.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago.

facts.heading: Running was a personal time
facts.content: Daniel felt running was the only time in the week nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Boss sends late night emails
facts.content: Daniel's boss, Peterson, sends emails at eleven at night. Peterson expects an answer before breakfast.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at eleven at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Answers all boss emails
facts.content: Daniel answers every email from his boss, even when he is in bed. Claire dislikes this habit.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss due to boss
facts.content: Daniel fears his boss will think he is not committed if he doesn't answer emails. He is afraid of being let go due to a restructuring in the spring.
facts.evidence: That he'd think I wasn't committed. There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Mortgage is a financial concern
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Moods are flat and irritable
facts.content: Daniel reports feeling flat and irritable, apart from the tiredness.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Snapped at colleague last week
facts.content: Daniel snapped at a colleague last week over nothing.
facts.evidence: I snapped at a colleague last week over nothing

facts.heading: Experienced physical symptoms in toilet
facts.content: While in the toilets, Daniel felt his heart going and his hands shaking. He thought it might be a heart attack.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking. I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Past frightening incidents
facts.content: Daniel has experienced frightening incidents a couple of times. One occurred on the train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: A couple of times. Once on the train to Manchester.

facts.heading: Kept incidents private
facts.content: Daniel has not told anyone about the frightening incidents, not even Claire.
facts.evidence: I haven't told anyone about it, not even Claire.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel fears that he is losing his mind and is not coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up like, I don't know. Not coping.

facts.heading: Caffeine intake amount
facts.content: Daniel consumes about six cups of coffee daily.
facts.evidence: I'm on about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Evening alcohol use
facts.content: Daniel has started drinking wine in the evenings, consuming two or sometimes three glasses.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Wine effect on sleep
facts.content: Daniel feels uneasy about the wine, noting it works for an hour before he wakes at three.
facts.evidence: Uneasy. It works for an hour and then I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Relief from sharing burdens
facts.content: Daniel felt a sense of relief after speaking about his issues in session.
facts.evidence: A bit of a relief, actually. Like putting down a bag I didn't realise I was carrying.

facts.heading: Sleep as primary need
facts.content: Daniel believes that if he could sleep, he could cope with other issues.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Family history of stoicism
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather and father both worked in mines and never complained about anything.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything, not once.

facts.heading: Daniel's perceived similarity to father
facts.content: Daniel feels he is the same as his father and believes one should just get on with things.
facts.evidence: I'm the same. I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Daniel's self-perception of tiredness
facts.content: Daniel states that he is not weak, but very tired.
facts.evidence: That I'm not weak. I'm just very tired.

facts.heading: Plan for evening phone break
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try turning off his phone at half past nine in the evening.
facts.evidence: Yes. Half past nine, perhaps.

facts.heading: Evening break with Claire
facts.content: Daniel plans to make the phone break routine with Claire, involving tea on the sofa.
facts.evidence: I could make it a thing with Claire. Tea on the sofa.

facts.heading: Plan to track sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel agreed to write down when he wakes up to track his night's sleep.
facts.evidence: I'll write down when I wake up, if I wake up.

facts.heading: Current feeling after session
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after the session.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter.

facts.heading: Next appointment scheduled
facts.content: Daniel confirmed he will attend the next session.
facts.evidence: Yes. I'll be here.

facts.heading: Trains are difficult for Daniel
facts.content: Daniel mentioned that the trains are awful.
facts.evidence: the trains are awful.
